docs.title: GitHub API Documentation
docs.text: This documentation introduces basic concepts of the GitHub API. It is intended for beginners who want to understand what the API does and how to interact with it. You can explore endpoints related to authentication, repositories, users, and issues.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication ensures that GitHub knows who you are. Without authentication, you can only access public data. Use a personal access token (PAT) to authenticate.

GET /user
Authorization: token YOUR_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
Issues are used to track tasks, enhancements, and bugs for your projects. They can be created, labeled, and assigned to collaborators. Here’s how to get a repository’s issues:

GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
A repository is a storage space for your project. It contains all of your project’s files and revision history. You can list a user's repositories like this:

GET /users/{username}/repos

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
A user represents a person or organization on GitHub. Each user has a profile and can own repositories. You can get information about a user with:

GET /users/{username}
